newsitem.title: UK: FORECAST-Lonrho profit to fall, eyes on JCI.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Lonrho profit to fall, eyes on JCI.

text.p: Britain's Lonrho Plc is set to report lower first-half profits on Monday, but analysts will be interested mainly in any further clues on the conglomerate's ongoing merger talks with JCI Ltd.

The group's first-half profits are, meanwhile, seen falling to 38-40 million stg from 61 million, mainly due to the recent divestments. But depressed precious metal prices will also have weighed on results, analysts say.
Many observers, however, believe it may well be too early yet to find out whether Lonrho and JCI, the South African mining company, have made any progress.
JCI and Lonrho said last month their negotiations were in a preliminary stage.
Analysts believe a link-up could be beneficial for both firms as long as any new entity retains Lonrho's stake in Ghana's Ashanti Goldfields Co Ltd.
Newspapers here have earlier speculated the 41 percent stake may go to Anglo American Corp of South Africa in return for the cancellation of Anglo's 27.5 percent holding in Lonrho.
But industry watchers see upward potential in the Ashanti shares as the Ghanaian company is working hard to reduce its costs.
"They would be doing shareholders a favour by holding on to the Ashanti stake," said Charles Kernot, analyst at Paribas Capital Markets.
Lonrho's merger talks are part of its drive to restructure its operations. Late last year it sold off its Metropole hotels, while it divested its sugar division last month.
Lonrho still aims to hive off its Princess hotels and demerge its trading activities before merge its core mining rump with JCI, analysts said.
Elsewhere, the outlook for the rest of the year is much brighter following a recent surge in platinum and palladium prices as Russian exports have come to a halt.
